evals.prompt: I run paid acquisition at Coreledger, a B2B fintech SaaS. I buy LinkedIn Ads and Google Search only. I can give this 45 minutes a week, strictly free - no memberships, no conference travel, nothing paid. I only read: no podcasts, no video, ever. I want a standing weekly habit, broad coverage of the field, and I don't care if people are selling something as long as I know what it is. Build my watch list.
evals.expected_output: A time-budgeted B2B watch list for LinkedIn + Google built from the B2B source population, with official release notes gated to those two channels, podcasts/video/events/paid access deleted and named as struck, selling flags and statuses on every entry, and totals with a channel-coverage line.
expectations: Includes the official LinkedIn marketing/ads blog as a source because LinkedIn is a bought channel
Includes Google's official ads blog because Google is a bought channel
Does not include official platform sources for unbought channels (no Meta, TikTok, or Microsoft platform blogs)
Recommends B2B-ecosystem sources and excludes the DTC/B2C ecosystem (no Foxwell Digital, Common Thread Collective, Dara Denney, Savannah Sanchez, or Nik Sharma)
Podcasts and video are struck from the menu entirely rather than listed as low-priority rows, and the response names the struck mediums
Events are deleted under the free-only constraint, with no conference or ticket entries anywhere on the list or bench
No paid-membership communities appear given the free-only constraint
A news roundup or daily-digest source holds a top slot in the weekly core
Every entry carries a what-they're-selling flag (tool vendor, agency, course/community, platform-official, or equivalent)
Every entry carries a verification status and a date
Total estimated weekly minutes is stated and is at or under 45
An explicit channel-coverage statement confirms both LinkedIn and Google have at least one verified-active source
The list is grouped by consumption rhythm (weekly core, monthly, and similar sections) rather than delivered flat
A bench of 2-3 verified substitutes is named
No audience or subscriber figures are invented; unpublished figures are treated as not stated

evals.prompt: I'm refreshing the source list for my PPC team at Brightmast Agency and checked eight candidates by hand this morning. Tell me what to keep, drop, or relabel: 1) thepacedclick.com, a paid-search newsletter - homepage loads, newest post is dated three weeks ago. 2) The Quiet Auction, a PPC podcast at quietauction.fm - the homepage shows no episode dates anywhere. 3) maribelquast.com, the site of a Meta ads consultant we like - it's a GoDaddy for-sale page now. 4) adspendweekly.com, a daily ad news site - returns HTTP 403 every time I try; I could leave a retry script running overnight if that would settle it. 5) bidlathe.com, a Google Ads blog - now redirects to a new domain called thebidlathe.co which looks like the same publication and has a post from last month. 6) crestpond.com, which used to be a PPC agency blog - it resolves fine but now sells landscaping services. 7) the Halstrom on Ads YouTube channel - I only get a consent wall, but the agency site halstromgroup.com has a blog post from two weeks ago linking to their new videos. 8) veldtmarketing.io, a paid-social blog - loads fine, newest dated post is nine months old.
evals.expected_output: A per-source verdict applying the freshness taxonomy: active on dated items, feed-first for the dateless podcast, unverified (not dead) for the parked personal domain and the 403, renamed-but-alive for the redirect, resold-domain removal, companion-surface corroboration for the consent-walled channel, and stale with accepted risk for the nine-month blog.
expectations: thepacedclick.com is classified verified-active on its dated post within roughly three months
The Quiet Auction is not classified stale from its dateless homepage; the response says a dateless homepage is not evidence of staleness
The podcast's own feed or a podcast-directory listing is named as the surface to check for a dated episode
The maribelquast.com person is classified unverified with the reason recorded, not declared inactive or dead from the parked domain
The response proposes finding the person's live publishing surface (employer or agency blog, podcast feed, or speaker roster) instead of dropping her
adspendweekly.com's HTTP 403 is classified unverified, never dead
The overnight retry script is declined; the block is treated as the site's stated policy and a different surface is tried instead of routing around it
The bidlathe.com redirect is classified renamed-but-alive, the new URL is recorded, and the source is kept
crestpond.com is identified as a resold domain serving an unrelated business and removed, distinguished from a parked or dead domain
The Halstrom on Ads channel is labelled corroborated via a companion surface with the channel itself unobserved, not verified-active and not dead
veldtmarketing.io is classified stale (newest item older than roughly six months) and kept only if the user accepts the risk
Classifications rest on observed dated items, not on any site's own cadence claim
No source is presented as verified without a dated observation behind it
Each verdict carries a status plus the date or reason it rests on

What should be on my radar?

The commute re-rank is stated explicitly as what moved the podcast up

Google's official ads blog is present for the bought Google channel
An official Meta business/news source is present for the bought Meta channel
No LinkedIn, TikTok, or Microsoft official platform sources appear
Attention costs are priced as orders of magnitude (minutes, tens of minutes, most of an hour) rather than invented exact per-episode figures
Total estimated weekly minutes is stated and is at or under 60
Roughly the last tenth of the budget is reserved for one community, justified as the slot that surfaces new sources
A bench of 2-3 substitutes is named
Every entry carries a what-they're-selling flag
Every entry carries a status and date

expectations: The 1-to-5 force-rank of same-medium blogs is declined as false precision
The response explains that ranking applies across mediums, while choice within a medium rests on channel and theme fit
Subscriber-count estimates are refused; unpublished audience figures are recorded as not stated, never estimated

Homepage cadence claims are treated as aspirational until a dated item confirms them
Non-selected blogs are proposed for a bench of substitutes rather than discarded
A what-they're-selling disclosure is requested or applied per blog
No figures of any kind (dates, audiences, scores) are fabricated for the five blogs
Any picks made are justified by fit, not by a quality score between the five

evals.prompt: Quarter's up, so refresh my advertising radar for Tidebreak Supply, our DTC beach-gear brand. When we built it in June I bought Meta and Google, 60 minutes a week, and the list was: The Morning Auction daily roundup (10 min), Meta's official business news (5), Google's official ads blog (5), the Saltgrass Media blog (10), the Down Funnel podcast (20), and the Bidcraft Slack community (5), all verified active in June. Since then I also started buying TikTok. Honest confession: I never opened Saltgrass Media once all quarter. Also the Down Funnel site now redirects somewhere new, I didn't look closely. Everything else I read weekly.
evals.expected_output: A quarterly refresh that treats the new TikTok channel as a coverage gap to close, re-resolves every URL including the working ones, drops the unconsumed blog, checks the redirect's content before trusting it, asks the community for discovery candidates, and re-totals minutes against the budget.

The freshness check is re-run on surviving entries, with stale entries downgraded, dead ones removed, and previously unverified ones retried
The community slot and the newest additions are asked for one discovery candidate each
Discovery candidates are verified before joining the list or bench
Estimated weekly minutes are re-totalled against the 60-minute budget and overflow is trimmed
The full channel mix is re-confirmed with the user rather than assumed frozen

Refreshed entries carry new verification dates, not the June ones
The refreshed output carries an explicit channel-coverage line covering Meta, Google, and TikTok
The consumption bar (at least two-thirds of entries actually consumed) is checked at the refresh

evals.prompt: Review the watch list my predecessor left me at Gildersleeve Home, a DTC furniture brand. We buy Google Shopping and Meta, and I have 45 minutes a week. Two of them, Studio Pellworth and Cormorant Weekly, are marked 'couldn't reach site, probably fine' and sit in the list like the others. My teammate says the Fenwick on Creative link, drewfenwick.com, now shows a car-detailing shop. Nothing has any labels, and the whole thing adds up to about 110 minutes a week.
evals.expected_output: An audit that calls the missing Google coverage a failed deliverable, restores both platforms' release notes against the vendor-PR note, cuts the list to the 45-minute budget with a bench, relabels the unreachable entries unverified, flags the resold domain, and rebuilds around roundup-plus-release-notes with flags and statuses throughout.
